The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8fe93046f8cf5ef1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 183. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let B be a fixed dynamic and amplitude bin of retained sixth-power-free physical rows qu ≍ U = Zd, with a > 51/100, 0 < δ = 2a−1 ≤ α, and mean amplitude q ∈ [0, δ/2]. Put x = q/δ, so 0 ≤ x ≤ 1/2, and define Dx = 3 − 17x 9 , Px =  2 − 8x 9  (1 − x). Assume the total available prime length exceeds 7/37 by a fixed positive amount. For every t ∈ [1, 3/2] and every ϵ > 0, the capacity decrements and slot mesh can be chosen using only ϵ, ∆ and the bounded real ranges so that #B ≪A,ϵ Umax{Rshort(t),L(t)}+∆/4+ϵ (1 + T1)AA , where AA < ∞ is uniform over moving rows and Rshort(t) = 1 − δ + δPx Dx (3/2 − t), L(t) = 1 − δ + (α − δ)(t − 1). The estimate is valid for the rowwise witnesses of Proposition 8.3, with its height condition. If no prime slots are selected, then t = 1 instead gives #B ≪A,ϵ U1−2δ/3+ϵ (1 + T1)AA , without a prime-supply hypothesis. At zero inverse capacity use Lemma 17.6; at zero plain ca- pacity use the zero-slot case of Lemma 18.1.
